trace.title: Single-agent loop · research task
trace.task: Find the population of the three largest cities in Japan and return them as a JSON object.

steps.content: I need three largest Japanese cities by population. I'll search, then fetch each city's population, then assemble JSON.
web_search({ query: 'largest cities in Japan by population' })

args.query: largest cities in Japan by population

result.title: List of cities in Japan by population

steps.content: All three populations retrieved. Assembling JSON object as requested.

gotchas.title: Missing max-iter cap
gotchas.symptom: Agent loops indefinitely when a tool keeps returning ambiguous results — burns budget, eventually times out.
gotchas.fix: Hard cap iterations (e.g. 8–12). On hit, emit an explicit 'max-iter' error step and return partial state instead of looping further.

gotchas.title: No JSON-parse fallback
gotchas.symptom: Model returns a tool call with malformed JSON args; loop crashes instead of recovering.
gotchas.fix: Wrap arg parsing in try/catch. On parse failure, feed the error back as a tool_result so the model can self-correct on the next turn.

gotchas.title: Tool result silently truncated
gotchas.symptom: A large tool result is cut at 4KB, model reads partial data and answers wrong, with high confidence.
gotchas.fix: Truncate explicitly with a visible '[truncated: N more bytes]' marker. Better: paginate via a follow-up tool call (`page_token`).

gotchas.title: Unbounded conversation context
gotchas.symptom: After 30+ steps, latency and cost balloon; relevant early facts get displaced by late noise.
gotchas.fix: Compact every N steps: summarize older tool results, keep IDs/references, drop verbose payloads. Cache breakpoints on the system prompt + tool defs to amortize.

gotchas.title: Tool errors returned as plain text
gotchas.symptom: A 500 from `lookup_population` is appended as a normal tool_result; model treats the error string as data and hallucinates around it.
gotchas.fix: Distinguish error from success in the tool_result envelope (`{ ok: false, error: '...' }`). Model is far better at handling structured errors than free-text apology strings.

gotchas.title: Model declares done too early
gotchas.symptom: After getting Tokyo only, model emits the final answer claiming all three are 'roughly the same'.
gotchas.fix: Validate the final answer against the task requirements before accepting. If schema-validated, the parse failure forces another loop turn.
